previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with a history of cholangiocarcinoma and biliary stents, was admitted for observation after experiencing bleeding during a routine ERCP stent clean-out. The bleeding, likely due to tumor ingrowth near the stent, slowed but did not fully stop, prompting hospitalization. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout the stay, with no signs of active bleeding, stable hemoglobin, and normal liver function tests. He received one dose of IV meropenem during the procedure and continued on suppressive delafloxacin. His diet was advanced without issue, and he was discharged home the following morning with plans for a repeat ERCP in three months and instructions to monitor for signs of bleeding or infection.

2. Similar appearance of an atrophic left hepatic lobe with mild intrahepatic
ductal dilatation bilaterally and new moderate-severe pneumobilia on the left,
likely sequela from the recent procedure.  No perihepatic fluid.  Dual CBD
stents appear in similar position to prior.
3. Multiple hypodensities within the liver, the largest measures 2.6 cm near
the right hepatic vein, some of which are new from the prior study, may
represent spread of disease versus sequela from cholangitis, however no active
extravasation or significant enhancement is demonstrated.

INDICATION:  ___ male with a PMH of cholangiocarcinoma (s/p chemo and
XRT, last in ___, follows w/ oncology, currently undergoing surveillance
only, no known recurrence), biliary obstruction c/b cholangitis requiring
metal stent placement and exchanges approximately every 2 months, Hx of MDR E
Coli bacteremia currently on suppressive delafloxacin, who presents with fever
to 103 at home concerning for recurrent cholangitis. s/p balloon sweep in ERCP
with hemorrhage of 1L blood from the biliary ducts. Pending possible ___
intervention of portobiliary fistula.

COMPARISON:  CTA abdomen and pelvis ___.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ Interventional ___ and
Dr. ___, Interventional Radiology fellow performed the procedure.
Dr. ___ supervised the trainee during any key components of
the procedure where applicable and reviewed and agrees with the findings as
reported below.
ANESTHESIA: General sedation was provided by anesthesia.
MEDICATIONS: Please see anesthesia note for medication details.
CONTRAST: 160 ml of Optiray contrast
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  23 minutes and 20 seconds, 365 mGy

PROCEDURE:  1. Ultrasound-guided access of the right posterior portal vein.
2. Portal venogram via transhepatic access.
3.  Cone beam CT portal venogram.
4.  Covered stent deployment in the main portal vein extending into the right
posterior portal vein.
5.  Post stenting cone beam CT portal venogram.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The abdomen was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Several ultrasound images were saved of the anterior and posterior portal vein
divisions as well as the ductal dilatation in the left hepatic lobe.  Color
Doppler images depicted turbulent flow at the stenosis of the right anterior
and posterior portal veins.  Under ultrasound guidance, a 21 gauge cook needle
was advanced into the a peripheral branch of the right posterior portal venous
system.  Contrast was injected under fluoroscopy to confirm positioning.  An
0.018 nitinol wire was advanced through the needle and into the main portal
vein.  The Cook needle was removed and a Accustick sheath and dilator were
advanced over the Nitinol wire.  Once within the portal system, the external
sheath was advanced off of the metal stylet and into the proximal right
posterior portal vein.  Contrast was injected to confirm positioning.  The
Accustick sheath was then advanced beyond the stenosis and into the main
portal vein over the Nitinol wire.  Contrast was injected to confirm position.
A dedicated portal venogram was performed.  This was followed by a cone beam
CT portal venogram.

Rotational cone-beam CT angiography was performed to help delineate the
anatomy, and particularly to identify the origin of the portal biliary
fistula.  Multiplanar CT images were reconstructed and 3D volume-rendered
images of the venous anatomy required post-processing on an independent
workstation under direct physician ___.  These images were used in the
interpretation, decision making for intervention and reporting of this
procedure.

An Amplatz wire was advanced through the Accustick sheath.  The sheath was
then exchanged for a 8 ___ sheath which was positioned in the main portal
vein.  The inner stiffener was removed.  A 10 mm x 29 mm Viabahn VBX balloon
expandable covered stent was advanced over the Amplatz wire and positioned for
deployment over the location of the portal biliary fistula.  The balloon was
inflated and the stent was deployed; however, the stenotic portal vein caused
the stent to slowly migrate towards main portal vein.  12 mm and followed by
14 mm atlas balloon catheters were used to dilate the stent further, but this
only caused further stent migration into the main portal vein.  The balloon
catheter was removed.

The 8 ___ sheath was then exchanged for a 12 ___ sheath.  The inner
stiffener was removed and a 13 mm x 5 cm Viabahn stent was advanced over the
Amplatz wire.  This stent was positioned such that it would overlap with the
previous stent and also span the stenosis of the right posterior portal vein,
excluding the portal biliary fistula and consequentially excluding the left
portal vein and right anterior portal vein.  The stent was deployed under
fluoroscopic surveillance and was not dilated.  The stent deployment device
was removed.  A straight flush catheter was advanced over the Amplatz wire. 
The wire was removed and contrast was injected to confirm position.  A post
stenting portal venogram was performed.  This was followed by a cone beam CT
portal venogram.

The Amplatz wire was removed.  The 12 ___ sheath was retracted to the
location of the access site.  The 12 ___ sheath was then cut and loaded
with several Gel-Foam pledgets.  The Gel-Foam pledgets were advanced with a
pusher and deployed in the access tract.  After the sheath was removed, an
ultrasound was performed at the access site to demonstrate hemostasis and
proper Gel-Foam pledgets deployment.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
post-procedure complications. The patient was transferred to the PACU in
stable condition.

FINDINGS: 

1.  Cone beam CT portal venogram revealed the portal biliary fistula to be in
close proximity to the left, right anterior and right posterior portal vein
origins.  The CT also revealed severe stenosis of the left and right anterior
and right posterior portal vein origins.
2.  Successful deployment of a covered stent spanning the main portal vein to
the right posterior portal vein, affectively excluding the portal biliary
fistula as well as the left portal vein and right anterior portal vein.
3.  Post stenting cone beam CT demonstrated resolution of the portal biliary
fistula as well as improved diameter of the right anterior portal vein origin.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful transhepatic access of the right posterior portal venous system and
deployment of a covered stent spanning the main portal vein to the right
posterior portal vein to exclude the portobiliary fistula.
